chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Charlie Parker locking himself in the men's room
summary: Opposite Collins's group, Parker played eight choruses then gave himself a fix in the men's room, and the door had to be broken down.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And so consequently we worked opposite all of the jazz groups. Bird -- did I mention I worked opposite Bird there? Well, any way, I don't know whether I told this story before, but if I did you stop me. Bird had the band, I think it was Bird and Red Rodney at this time. And they were the two horns. So Bird would -- this particular night Bird came on, and played about eight choruses right away, just first he got on and he really cooked. And he got off the stand and then Red started to solo. And right opposite the bandstand was the men's room, and Bird went in the men's room and locked the door and gave himself a fix and fell out. Nobody could get in the men's room. We had to break the door down, to get in there, to get in the men's room. You know.
But also Sid Catlett had a band, after Bird, and this was John Simmons, and I don't know who all. A very good band.
